shots.title: Contain the Failure
shots.visualGoal: Mitigation decisions: do not misrepresent as database cure.
shots.startingFrame: Single map remains. Use local overlays at the right intervention point rather than five unrelated slides. Toggle each intervention deliberately while maintaining DB cap context.
shots.cameraDirection: Medium full map → local interventions/mini-worlds → Wide comparative before/contained state without fake total recovery.
shots.assetDirection: Reuse paths, pool, failure state; propose RetryBudgetGate, BackoffJitterTimeline, EarlyRejectGate, CircuitBreaker, EnforcedBulkhead6plus2.
shots.truthContinuity: Mitigations do not upgrade DB capacity. Some users fail quickly, some succeed conditionally. Not presented as an observed production recovery.
shots.transition: Remove intervention overlays and move to measurable user outcomes.

beats.direction: First isolate retry side path and attach `RETRY BUDGET`. At limit, refuse extra safe lookup attempts. Keep new-Login arrival count independent.
Then animate deterministic stepped delay windows `BACKOFF` with slight per-attempt offsets `JITTER` on read-only retry arrows, not on credential Login posts.

At `load shedding`, position early admission gate before expensive DB-dependent work: some new Logins fail quickly and clearly. Avoid treating this as successful authentication or as improvement for every user.

At `circuit breaker`, pause new database calls under modeled severe failures; show fail-closed Login response, then a limited safe test window to probe recovery; never issue a successful session without account proof.

At `bulkhead isolation`, zoom into a configurable Auth pool max8 and present a PROPOSED split `6 • new Login lookups | 2 • read-only retries`, as an illustrative enforced reservation, not just eight free-floating slots.

At `waiting line can finally start to shrink`, conditionally reduce backlog ONLY when admitted total DB demand including retries falls below sustainable completed throughput. Keep DB capacity value unchanged.
Maintain consistent camera landmarks so viewers can tell budget/backoff/admission/breaker/bulkhead operate at different boundaries, not one magic `FIX` state.

beats.direction: On `full Login journey`, zoom from Phone into widest legible architecture; remove secondary meters until only critical route remains.

At `lookups slowed`, highlight saturated-but-running DB; at `connections stayed busy`, light Auth01 pool; at `requests waited`, show bounded queue; at `deadlines expired`, mark an expired request, not the DB as dead.
At `servers still running`, keep green probe marker but display incomplete Login journey. On protection recap, bring back lightweight boundary indicators without claiming higher DB throughput.
At `a healthy server doesn't guarantee`, hold the full map and visual dual signal `SERVER UP / LOGIN NOT GUARANTEED`, avoiding decorative confetti or fictitious recovery.

At `database itself needs more capacity?`, gently isolate User Database and darken other components; let the question hang. `That's where our next story begins` becomes an editorial cut, not an explanation of replica topology or next episode script.
